explanation: Supergroup Archaeplastida includes land plants and other photosynthetic organisms that contain plastids derived from cyanobacteria. This group features red and green algae, which contain chlorophyll a and b. Green algae are split into two groups: 1) Chlorophytes, such as Chlamydomonas (exhibits a sexual life cycle), Volvox (colonial), and Ulva (multicellular); and 2) Charophytes, which are filamentous algae that are most closely related to land plants, including Spirogyra and Chara. Red algae contain red and blue accessory pigments and have various commercial uses, including the production of agar (lab substrate), carrageenan extracts (used in chocolate and cosmetics), and Porphyra (seaweed wrappings for sushi).

questions.q: Which green algae group is most closely related to land plants?
questions.exp: The notes state that Charophytes are filamentous and 'most closely related to land plants'.
The notes state: 'Porphyra used for seaweed wrappings on sushi'.

questions.exp: The notes list 'Ulva-multicellular' as a Chlorophyte green algae.
